pattern.yes: magnitude (where interpretable) → difficulty checklist → topography/extras → optional example → Step-3 depth
pattern.no: strengths / current-functioning checklist (optional, with nudge) → optional data point
pattern.not_observed: no checklist; observation gap preserved explicitly
pattern.nudge: Select any statements or data that describe the student's current functioning. If none are selected, the section will state only that no concerns were reported.
pattern.uncheckedNote: Check all that apply. Leave an item unchecked if it does not apply, you have not observed it, or you are unsure — an unchecked item is never read as either a strength or a difficulty.

outputLicensing.licenses: “No concerns were reported in this area at this time.” Nothing further.
A short affirmative paragraph built only from what was selected, followed by that same conclusion.
An attributed concern paragraph using only the specifics given — never escalated in severity, frequency, or cause.
“Not enough opportunity to observe was reported by this informant.” Never rendered as no concern, and never used to check the district's N box.

removed: The one fixed checklist shown regardless of disposition
The master “which areas are concerning” checklist (TCH-CORE-008)
The derived concern-set machinery, provenance tracking, and the two affirmative screeners
The twelve reconciliation completeness rules (CR-010 … CR-021)
Vision/hearing screening availability as a teacher checklist item
The editable grade question (case grade is displayed read-only)
The five-question ABC interview repeated for every behavior topography
The nine uniform comparison scales of v1.5.0 (kept only where interpretable)

openQuestions.topic: Taxonomy gap — speech fluency and voice
openQuestions.detail: The district asks about stuttering (repetitions, prolongations, blocks) and voice quality (nasal, hoarse, breathy). The taxonomy has LANG.ARTIC but no construct for either. Those two items are tagged to the parent LANG and marked — they need a taxonomy v0.5 addition before this becomes a bank, or their evidence will be under-specified.

openQuestions.topic: Placement of the two context items
openQuestions.detail: The regression and attendance questions are drafted at the end of Step 1. They are about the student rather than about your work, so they may belong at the head of Step 2 instead. Placement affects nothing downstream — your call.

Nine peer-comparison questions are proposed, one per domain where comparison is interpretable (all except Sensory, Vision & Hearing, and Other). Each appears only when that domain is marked as a concern. Confirm the set, or strike any that read as forced.

This draft contains roughly 121 checklist statements plus the scales and follow-ups. Every one is draft content authored against the district arrangement — they determine what evidence the product actually elicits and need item-by-item practitioner review before any of this becomes a published bank.
